findings.finding: From the company's own capacity disclosures, Q3 revenue lands around $56-62M, roughly in line with to ~6% below the $63-64M consensus. HPC lease revenue was $21.0M at 60 MW (Q1) and $31.9M with 81 MW at June 30 (Q2). 102 MW was running for the whole of Q3 after CB-3 was delivered in early July, which implies about $44-49M of HPC revenue. Mining revenue ($13.0M in Q1, $12.8M in Q2) is likely $10-14M because capacity is being repurposed.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Confirmed earnings releases (rebuilt from SEC 8-Ks, not the contaminated baseline): Q2 2026 on 2026-08-05 missed revenue ($44.8M vs ~$46-48M), stock -4.29%. Q1 2026 on 2026-05-08 missed revenue estimates, -2.62%. Q4 2025 on 2026-02-26, -9.28%. Q3 2025 on 2025-11-10, -13.5%. Q2 2025 on 2025-08-08, +1.82%. Four of five down, median |move| 4.3%.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus at $63-64M (high $79.5M, Earnings Whispers $72.2M) suggests part of the street models CB-4 rent in Q3 or higher mining revenue. If the market had priced a light quarter, the top of the estimate range would have been cut toward $60M. It has not been.
findings.independence: Q1 2026 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001083301/000108330126000083/a_wulfearningsreleaseq1202.htm) for the per-MW run-rate. The Earnings Whispers preview (https://www.earningswhispers.com/article/WULF/22508) notes CB-4 was due at quarter-end and 'should add little revenue'. This is my inference from the company's MW data, not a company number.

findings.finding: The Google warrant liability ($1,816.7M at June 30 on about 77.7M warrants with a $0.10 strike) is remeasured from a $24.70 close on June 30 to a $14.80 close on Sept 30 (-40%). That implies a non-cash gain on the order of $700M in Q3. Headline GAAP EPS should print around +$1.3-1.5 against consensus of -$0.09 to -$0.38, the mirror of Q2's -$1.94 'miss' caused by a $755.7M warrant loss.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: the $755.7M warrant loss produced a headline 'misses by $1.70' (MarketBeat 2026-08-05), and the stock fell only 4.29% alongside a revenue miss, so the market looked through most of it. Peer CIFR posted GAAP net income from a warrant gain on 2026-11-02 alongside a 29% revenue miss.
findings.why_not_priced: Every consensus source still shows a GAAP loss for Q3 (-$0.09 to -$0.38), so the headline-EPS tape will print a large 'beat'. Sophisticated holders know it is non-cash, which is why it is sized small. It changes no guidance.
findings.independence: Closing prices from Yahoo chart API (https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/WULF?period1=1790294400&period2=1790985600&interval=1d : 2026-09-30 close $14.80; June 30 close $24.70 from the same API). The Earnings Whispers preview flags that headline EPS could swing on non-operating items.

findings.finding: CB-4 (168 MW at Lake Mariner) was last guided to energize its first data hall and start rent in late September 2026. Since the Q2 call, none of the company's three subsequent releases (Muskie 2026-10-05, revolver amendment 2026-10-23, Hawesville financing 2026-11-04) confirms that the handover happened. Each earlier building slipped: CB-3 from 'May 2026' (Q1 release) to early July; CB-5 from '2026' to early 2027; CB-4 from Q3 to late September. The call's statement on CB-4 and CB-5 timing is the main swing factor for the $102M Q4 consensus.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q2 2026 call (2026-08-05) carried the CB-5 slip to early 2027 and the CB-4 slip to late September, and the stock fell 4.29%. The CB-3 slip from May to early July was disclosed with the Q2 numbers.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the stock is -60% since June and -27.5% since the last call. But the Q4 revenue consensus still averages $102M with a high of $138M, which assumes CB-4 rent through Q4. If a further slip were priced, Q4 estimates would sit nearer the $66.6M low. The sign is uncertain: an on-time CB-4 would be a positive of similar size.
findings.independence: Q1 2026 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001083301/000108330126000083/a_wulfearningsreleaseq1202.htm: 'CB-3 capacity in May 2026', 'CB-4 and CB-5 remain on schedule for delivery and rent commencement in 2026'). Q2 release (CB-5 early 2027). Earnings Whispers preview (https://www.earningswhispers.com/article/WULF/22508) on the slipping timelines. Baxtel 2026-03-20 (https://baxtel.com/news/terawulf-completes-latest-data-center-at-new-york-s-lake-mariner-campus): CB-4 168 MW topped out, energization slated for Q3 2026. The 'no announcement' part is inference from absence, so it is sized small.

findings.finding: Q2 HPC segment margin fell to about 28% from about 50% (long-term target ~85%), adjusted EBITDA was -$18.3M, and build cost was about $9.1M per MW against a guided $8-10M range. Q3 carries the full-quarter revenue of CB-3's capacity with little new pre-opening load beyond CB-4 commissioning, so adjusted EBITDA should narrow.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026's EBITDA swing to -$18.3M (from +$14.5M a year earlier) came with a -4.29% reaction. No clean prior case of a margin recovery.
findings.why_not_priced: The margin story is in the preview, so the direction is known. What is not priced is the size: if CB-4 commissioning and Kentucky pre-development costs kept EBITDA negative, the improvement could be nil. Kept small because it is an inference about the quarter.
findings.independence: Q2 2026 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001083301/000108330126000162/a_wulfearningsreleaseq22026.htm) gives adjusted EBITDA -$18.3M. This shares the Q2 document with finding 1.

findings.finding: The seal-day selloff (-13.5%, 'AI data-center regulation fears') follows the 2026-11-04 Texas election headlines: Bernstein cut targets on seven miners, and Cipher fell 17% then 20.5%. But WULF's operating and contracted footprint is in New York and Kentucky, and it agreed in July to sell its only Texas asset (the 50.1% Abernathy JV, $530M to a Fluidstack-led group). Rosenblatt picked TeraWulf on 2026-11-04 on that basis. The call can restate that it has no ERCOT exposure.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: July 2026: New York's data-center permit pause cost the stock 7% the same day even though the company said its projects were unaffected (crowdfundinsider 2026-07). Sector contagion has hit this name before regardless of exposure.
findings.why_not_priced: If the market were separating Texas exposure, WULF would have held up relative to CIFR on Nov 4-5. Instead it fell about 13.5% on the 5th, close to CIFR's -12.4% intraday. This is sector-to-company transmission plus a company document, so it is sized small.
findings.independence: finviz news list 2026-11-04 (https://finviz.com/quote.ashx?t=WULF): 'Rosenblatt picks TeraWulf as Democratic wins raise the value of permitted MW', 'Cipher Mining sinks 17% as Texas election puts AI data-center expansion at risk'. 247wallst CIFR card (https://247wallst.com/cards/cipher-digital-q3-2026-earnings-cifr-01m6e39m9jkttpk702rtfx3eex) for CIFR's moves.

findings.finding: Financing overhang: on 2026-11-04 Google signed credit support for the anticipated debt financing of the Hawesville campus (about $19B of Anthropic lease commitments, Fluor EPC, phased completions late 2027 to Q2 2028). The revolver was raised from $250M to about $400M on 2026-10-23. A large debt deal (about $3.5B reported in July) is likely soon and could be launched around the print. The money funds a contracted, Google-supported build, so this is not distress. The in-window risk is an equity or convertible tranche at the 52-week low.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 2026-04-14/15: an $800-900M common stock sale cost -6.11% (baseline row and Yahoo/Motley Fool 'TeraWulf Shares Fall After $900 Million Stock Sale'). The October 2025 $3.2B secured notes and $900M converts funded the Fluidstack build.
findings.why_not_priced: The Google support was announced on Nov 4, and the stock still fell 13.5% the next day, so the market has not credited it. Whether a debt-only package follows, or whether equity is needed for the equity share of a ~$9M/MW build, is unresolved. The sign depends on that answer, so the finding is near zero with a fat left tail.
findings.independence: Stocktwits 2026-10-24 on the revolver (https://stocktwits.com/news-articles/markets/equity/wulf-stock-hits-six-month-weekly-low-as-terawulf-secures-larger-credit-line-for-ai-data-center-expansion/cZUGAjERBU1). findings.finding: Muskie (eastern Kentucky) contracted power was raised from 500 MW to 1 GW under an amended Kentucky Power agreement executed 2026-10-01, with the second 500 MW phase pulled forward from 2030 to 2029, subject to Kentucky PSC approval. This adds pipeline the call can point to against a 250-500 MW-a-year signing target that has been reaffirmed but not raised.

findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: it was public a month ago and sold. It matters only if a tenant is named on the call.

Hawesville/Justified debt financing close (Google credit support signed 2026-11-04; amount undisclosed), with phased ready-for-service from late 2027. A close is unlikely inside one session.

baseline_tension: The evidence cuts both ways against the baseline. The revenue lean and the CB-4 uncertainty agree with the +5.18 put skew and the -21% run-in, while the 36.7% short interest and the Texas contagion argue the run-in overshot. Net, I see no edge over the option market on direction.
lessons_applied: Lesson 2 (one-offs): the Google warrant remeasurement gain is below operating income with no path to guidance, cut from +0.5 to +0.3
Lesson 4 (financing is a question): the money buys a contracted, Google-supported Anthropic build, so the financing finding moved from -0.5 to -0.2, with the left tail kept for an equity tranche
Lesson 7 (crowded short shrinks negatives): with 36.7% of float short, the CB-4 negative was cut from -1.0 to -0.7 and the revenue negative from -0.5 to -0.4
Lesson 5 (absence is not a cause / proxy transmission): the 'no CB-4 announcement' element stays small, and the Texas-contagion finding was cut from +0.8 to +0.5 as sector-to-company transmission
Lesson 3 (own caveat reaches the number): the margin finding's own caveat (Kentucky and CB-4 pre-opening costs) cut it from +0.5 to +0.3

Core sweep rule plus the lesson on wrong-event history: the base rate was rebuilt from five confirmed releases (4 of 5 down, median |4.3%|), which together with the put skew moved p_up from 52 to 50 and abs_move from 12 to 11
Core step 2 (file everything sourced): the Muskie 1 GW item was added as a +0.1 finding instead of being left unfiled
The sum stays +1.3 after revision (the composition changed, the total did not); the scaled number moved from +0.48 to 0
